# ZVect

> A tiny vector library for learning, in three languages with the same API:
> JavaScript (ES module), Python (standard library only) and C++17 (header-only).
> Zero dependencies. A vector is a plain list of numbers.
> License: ZVect Non-Commercial Study License — study and experiments only,
> no commercial use without written permission (see LICENSE).

## Files (copy one file, nothing else is needed)

- [zvect.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zardokar/ZVect/main/lib/zvect.js): JavaScript, Node >= 18 or browser, `import { cosine } from "./zvect.js"`
- [zvect.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zardokar/ZVect/main/lib/zvect.py): Python 3, `from zvect import cosine`
- [zvect.hpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zardokar/ZVect/main/lib/zvect.hpp): C++17, `#include "zvect.hpp"`, namespace `zv`, vector type `zv::Vec` (std::vector<double>)
- [MANIFEST.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zardokar/ZVect/main/lib/MANIFEST.json): version + sha256 of each file. Verify the file you fetched against it.

## API (same names in all three; Python uses top_k instead of topK)

- vec(...xs) -> vector
- add(a, b), sub(a, b), scale(a, k) -> vector
- dot(a, b) -> number            sum of a[i] * b[i]
- norm(a) -> number              length |a|
- normalize(a) -> vector         a / |a|, zero vector stays zero
- distance(a, b) -> number       |a - b|
- cosine(a, b) -> number         (a . b) / (|a| |b|), in [-1, 1], 0 if either is zero
- angle(a, b) -> radians         clamped, never NaN
- project(b, a) -> vector        projection of b onto a
- mean(list) -> vector           centroid
- topK(query, items, k=3, metric=cosine)
    JS:     items [{ id, v }]  -> [{ id, v, score }] best first
    Python: items [(id, v)]    -> [(id, score)] best first
    C++:    vector<pair<string, Vec>> -> vector<pair<string, double>>; metric is std::function
- classify(x, centroids, metric=cosine)   nearest centroid
    JS: { label: vector } -> { label, score }
    Python: dict -> (label, score)
    C++: vector<pair<string, Vec>> (ordered) -> pair<string, double>
- words(text) -> list            split on ASCII non-alphanumerics, lower-case A-Z only; non-ASCII (e.g. Thai) stays in words
- encode(text, table) -> unit vector      toy bi-encoder: mean of known word vectors, zero vector if none known

## Shared rules (enforced by tests/parity, identical in all three)

- size mismatch -> throws "size mismatch: n vs m" (JS Error, Python ValueError, C++ std::invalid_argument)
- mean([]) -> "empty list"; classify with no centroids -> "no centroids"; encode with empty table -> "empty table"
- cosine with a zero vector returns 0 (mathematically undefined; 0 by convention)
- a vector whose squared length underflows to 0 (e.g. [1e-300, 0, 0]) counts as a zero vector (cosine 0, normalize -> zero)
- ties: topK keeps input order, classify picks the first label
- fmt(x) -> string               3 decimals, "[1.000, 2.000]" (identical output in all three)
- VERSION

## Rules for AI agents using this repo

- Do not add dependencies or frameworks. Any exception needs a dated owner approval row in docs/APPROVALS.md.
- After editing lib/, run `npm run manifest`, `npm test` and `npm run check` (JS / Python / C++ outputs must match).
- The web lessons use dark theme only.

## Learn

- Lessons (online: https://zardokar.github.io/ZVect/ (GitHub Pages is on since 2026-10-11); locally: `npm start`, open http://localhost:5173), numbered chapter.topic: 1 basics (1.1 vector, 1.2 length, 1.3 vector space, 1.4 add/subtract/scale, 1.5 matrix = vectors as rows) | 2 closeness (2.1 Euclidean distance, 2.2 dot product, 2.3 cosine) | 3 tokens (text to ids) (3.1 tokenization: characters or words to vocabulary IDs, in EN / TH / ZH / JP, 3.2 BPE: merge the most frequent adjacent pair k times, 3.3 GPT tokenizer: byte-level BPE on UTF-8 bytes (Thai = 3 bytes per character, new ids 256 + i, encode oldest rule first, decode with errors="replace", optional GPT-2 split regex), 3.4 token ID) | 4 text embeddings (ids to meaningful vectors) (4.1 one-hot, 4.2 bag of words, 4.3 embedding matrix, 4.4 learning the table, 4.5 latent space, 4.6 same embedding model for query and documents (vectors from different models are not comparable), 4.7 static vs contextual embeddings (same word, different sentences)) | 5 nearest-item search (5.1 by cosine, 5.2 by distance, 5.3 by dot, 5.4 choosing a metric, 5.5 keyword (inverted index) vs meaning) | 6 fast search at scale: less work per item, simple to complex (6.1 brute force, 6.2 high dimensions, 6.3 1-bit vectors with XOR + popcount, 6.4 ANN random-split tree (Annoy)) | 7 graph search: one-layer walk to HNSW (7.1 one-layer neighbour-graph walk, 7.2 HNSW layered graph, 7.3 HNSW beam / efSearch, 7.4 HNSW layers by coin flip, 7.5 filtering breaks the graph below about 1/k) | 8 combining the theory (8.1 bi-encoder in EN / TH / ZH / JP: split at spaces vs dictionary longest match, 8.2 late interaction (ColBERT: one vector per token, MaxSim then sum, vs the bi-encoder), 8.3 reranker (cross-encoder) in four languages with per-language negation (not / ไม่ / 不 before the word, ない after), 8.4 classification) | 9 vectors in an LLM (9.1 embedding layer + positional encoding, 9.2 attention scores with query · key) | 10 Transformer theory (Stanford CME295) (10.1 why the Transformer (RNN hidden state vs direct attention), 10.2 self-attention softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V with mask, 10.3 sinusoidal position encoding, 10.4 transformer block (multi-head, residual, layer norm, FFN; encoder vs decoder)). File prefixes (01_…43_) are creation order; chapters and order live in web/data/chapters.json (edit it, then run `npm run reindex`).
- Sources the lessons draw on: REFERENCE.md. To save tokens read only its first part (topic groups + tag index), then jump with `grep -n "^## yt:<ref>" REFERENCE.md` or `grep -n "tags:.*<tag>" REFERENCE.md`; each source also has an English context file in docs/aimd/.
- Runnable examples: examples/js, examples/py, examples/cpp (same output in every language).

## LLM knowledge and the LLM manual (for sessions from other projects too)

- Start here: [docs/arch/WIP202610050_llm-manual/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zardokar/ZVect/main/docs/arch/WIP202610050_llm-manual/README.md): what the Thai LLM manual is, where its parts live, what to read per task, and the read-only rules for sessions from another project.
- The knowledge itself: docs/aimd/*_claude.md, 27 English notes (tokens, BPE, embeddings, transformer, fine-tuning, vector search, RAG); the A01–A27 map is in that folder's plan.md §3. Cite file + line when you reuse them.
- Current status is in checkpoints/checkpoint.zvect.ver002.md §6 (last section), not in any copy.
